core_obligations: Identify the I-adic completion with the limit of the quotients by the ideals generated by the n-th powers of the generators, using I^n contained in (f_1^n, ..., f_r^n) contained in I^{rn} (proof lines 22980-22981).
Write an element of that limit symbolically as a sum over n and i of f_i^n x_{n,i} with x_{n,i} in M (proof lines 22982-22986).
Use surjectivity onto each one-generator completion to find x_i mapping to the corresponding series, and observe that their sum maps to the given element (proof lines 22987-22989).
proof_roadmap: Replace the ideal-adic tower by the tower from the separate powers of the generators (proof lines 22979-22981).
Match the symbolic series term by term with the elements obtained from the one-generator hypotheses (proof lines 22982-22990).
difficulty_reason: For a finitely generated ideal I = (f_1, ..., f_r) the lemma states that if M surjects onto each completion with respect to a single generator, then M surjects onto the I-adic completion (statement lines 22972-22977). The proof does not argue with the I-adic filtration directly: it replaces it by the filtration cut out by the separate powers of the generators, using I^n contained in (f_1^n, ..., f_r^n) contained in I^{rn}, writes an element of the resulting limit as a symbolic series in the f_i, and matches the series term by term using the hypotheses for the individual generators (proof lines 22979-22990). The substitution of one tower by the other is the step that makes the term-by-term matching possible. H2.
